Subject: Azure private offer — PO & invoice routing question

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement here — a couple quick operational questions so we can route the PO internally:

- BrightBank wants the invoice to be issued to our remit-to address (see attached PO) and include our PO number 12345 on every invoice. Can Redwood invoice BrightBank directly for a private offer, or do we need to route billing through Microsoft/Azure?
- We need to confirm the company name/legal entity you will appear on the invoice, the tax ID, and remit-to address.
- Our standard payment terms are Net45. Would Redwood accept Net45 for an initial pilot?
- Finally, please confirm whether you can sign our DPA/Data Processing Exhibit or if we should expect to sign a Redwood-provided DPA amendment.

Attached: BrightBank_PO_12345.pdf (pdf)

Appreciate a short note on next steps — procurement is blocking approval until billing flow is clear.

Best,
Elena Ross

BrightBank

Subject: Re: Azure private offer — PO & invoice routing question

Hi Elena — thanks for sending the PO. Looping in Legal (Laura) and Revenue Ops (Aditya) to confirm the details. Short answers below, plus a suggested next step.

1) Invoice routing: For Azure Marketplace private offers we typically support two billing flows:
   - Azure-managed billing (customer billed by Microsoft; Microsoft remits to seller)
   - Merchant invoices (seller invoices customer directly) when the seller is onboarded as a merchant and the offer is configured for direct invoicing.

Given BrightBank's procurement controls it sounds like you prefer seller invoicing (direct) so the invoice can show your PO number and remit-to. We can do that, but it requires the private offer to be set to "seller invoice" mode and an amendment to the Marketplace listing. I attached a draft amendment that captures the invoice flow and the billing contact fields we need.

2) Legal / DPA: We can execute your DPA or present our standard Data Processing Exhibit tied to the private offer. Laura — can you confirm the preferred path?

3) Payment terms: We can accept Net45 for the pilot, subject to finance approval and the merchant onboarding checklist (tax docs, W-9). Aditya — can finance confirm?

Next steps (proposed):
- BrightBank confirms the remit-to address and whether PO 12345 is the only PO for Phase 1.
- Redwood returns signed amendment + DPA (or accepts BrightBank DPA) and onboarding docs.
- We provision the private offer in Azure with seller-invoice configuration.

Attaching: Redwood_Azure_Private_Amendment_v3.docx (docx) — draft with invoice routing language, pay-to, and tax fields.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if that helps move procurement along.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0110
From: Elena Ross <elena.ross@brightbank.com>

Subject: Re: Azure private offer — PO & invoice routing question

Jonas — thanks, that helps. A couple clarifications from procurement after reviewing the draft amendment:

- BrightBank will accept seller invoicing for the private offer if Redwood can issue invoices to: BrightBank Holdings, Inc.
  Remit-to: BrightBank AP, 800 Market St, Suite 300, San Francisco, CA 94102
  Please list PO #12345 on each invoice.
- Payment terms: Procurement's preference is Net45. We can accept Net30 for recurring billing only if Redwood offers a 1.5% early-pay discount for payment within 15 days; otherwise Net45 is standard for this buyer.
- Documents: We need Redwood's W-9 (or equivalent tax form) and a signed DPA. Also, BrightBank requests a limited IP escrow clause for critical production deployments — can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a narrow escrow (source for the runtime only, released on insolvency or perpetual breach) rather than a broad IP assignment?

I reattached our PO for completeness. If you can confirm the above and provide the W-9 and the amended Marketplace exhibit, procurement can issue a PO release.

Thanks,
Elena

Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace Private Offer — redlines and IP escrow

Elena / Jonas / team —

Thanks for the clear note. I reviewed BrightBank's procurement requests and the attached draft amendment. High level: we can accommodate most commercial asks but have a few redlines to propose so we can preserve Redwood's IP and limit exposure. Summary below: 

- Payment terms: Redwood accepts Net45 for Phase 1 pilot. If BrightBank requests an early-pay discount, we'll accept 1.5% for payments made within 15 days. Please confirm if procurement wants us to include that in the amendment.
- W-9 & tax: Redwood will provide a W-9 for Redwood Cloud, Inc. (EIN: 27-1234567). Finance to confirm remit-to name.
- IP escrow: We will accept a narrowly scoped escrow covering only the runtime artifacts required to operate the specific private offer. Escrow release triggers limited to (a) Redwood insolvency, (b) court-ordered release, or (c) material, uncured breach impacting production for 90+ days. We cannot accept broad source-code escrow or assignment.
- DPA: We can sign BrightBank's DPA with two redlines around subprocessors and audit scope. If BrightBank prefers, we can present our standard DPA exhibit that maps to the Azure private offer.

Attached: SOW-BrightBank-Phase1.pdf (pdf) — draft SOW for milestone billing and acceptance criteria.

If BrightBank confirms Net45, remit-to, and PO mapping, we can finalize the amendment and route the commercial signature. Proposed timeline: 3 business days for legal and 2 business days for finance onboarding once we have the signed amendment and W-9.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Elena — thanks for the confirmation and detail. Quick summary and next steps so procurement can close the loop: 

- Invoicing: Redwood will be the merchant invoicing BrightBank (seller invoice). We will update the Azure private offer to seller-invoice mode and include PO #12345 on all invoices. Finance will send the W-9 to procurement today.
- Payment terms: Redwood accepts Net45 for the pilot. If BrightBank wants an early-pay option, we can include a 1.5% discount for payments within 15 days — please confirm if you want that included in the amendment.
- IP escrow: Legal has agreed to a narrowly scoped escrow limited to runtime artifacts and with clearly defined release triggers (insolvency / court order / uncured material breach > 90 days). Laura will inline the escrow drafting into the Marketplace amendment.
- DPA: Laura will propose redlines to BrightBank's DPA; if you prefer our standard DPA, we can provide that instead.

Actions we will take now: 
1) Aditya will upload the signed amendment (once agreed) to DocuSign and send the envelope link.
2) Finance will upload W-9 and merchant onboarding documents to the secure Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=redwood-bb-priv-4521
3) We will update Jira with the deployment and billing tasks: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RB-4521 (owner: marissa_cole)

Can you confirm: (a) final remit-to address (as you'd like it printed), (b) whether to include the early-pay 1.5% clause, and (c) the correct AP contact for invoice submission? Once confirmed we will send the DocuSign envelope for commercial signature.

Thanks — looking forward to getting BrightBank onboarded.

Best,
Jonas
